a2Course.tipFutur: Futur I = werden + the base verb at the end: Ich werde morgen arbeiten. Forms: ich werde, du wirst, er/sie wird, wir werden, ihr werdet, sie/Sie werden. People often use the present instead: Morgen arbeite ich. Futur is used for promises, plans and guesses.
a2Course.tipPerfekt: Perfekt = haben or sein in second place + the participle at the end: Ich habe Brot gekauft. Wir sind nach Berlin gefahren. sein goes with verbs of movement and change of state: gehen, fahren, kommen, aufstehen. Participle: ge...t for regular verbs (gemacht), ge...en for strong verbs (gesehen). Verbs in be-, ver-, er- and -ieren have no ge-: bezahlt, studiert.

questionBridgeOne.questDescription: Many German verbs always come with their own preposition. You already know warten auf, sich freuen auf, Angst haben vor. New ones: denken an (to think of), sich interessieren für (to be interested in), sich kümmern um (to take care of), sich ärgern über (to be annoyed about). After these prepositions comes the accusative: an den Urlaub, um die Kinder. Learn the preposition together with the verb.

definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.title: Battle for Endings
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.description: Mixed practice: indefinite and definite articles in sentences.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.goal: Solidify the difference in endings using real phrases!
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questOne: Enter the form (alt): Dort steht ein ___ Haus.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questOneTip: Indefinite article (unknown object). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -es ending from the article 'das'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questTwo: Enter the form (alt): Das ___ Haus ist sehr schön.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questTwoTip: Definite article (specifically known object). The article 'das' already showed the gender, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questThree: Choose the correct option: I see a new TV
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questThreeTip: Indefinite article, masculine, Akkusativ. The article 'einen' already has an ending, so the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFour: Choose the correct option: I will buy this new TV
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFourTip: Definite article in Akkusativ. The article 'den' has changed, so the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFive: Assemble: A small cat is sitting in the garden
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFiveTip: Feminine. After the article 'eine', the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questSix: Assemble: This small cat is very cute
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questSixTip: The definite article 'die' already showed everything, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questSeven: Enter the form (gut): Er ist ein ___ Freund.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questSevenTip: Indefinite article (unknown object). Masculine (der). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -er ending from the article 'der'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questEight: Enter the form (gut): Der ___ Freund hat mir geholfen.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questEightTip: Definite article (specifically known). The article 'der' already showed the gender, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questNine: Choose the correct option: We ate a tasty ice cream
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questNineTip: Neuter (das Eis). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -es ending from the article 'das'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questTen: Choose the correct option: This tasty ice cream was cold
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questTenTip: The article 'das' already showed the neuter gender, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questEleven: Assemble: I will buy a new laptop
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questElevenTip: Masculine, Akkusativ. The article 'einen' has an ending, so the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questTwelve: Assemble: I met that very old neighbor
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questTwelveTip: Akkusativ, masculine. After the article 'den', the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questThirteen: Enter the form (neu): Das ist ein ___ Computer.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questThirteenTip: Indefinite article. Masculine (der). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -er ending from the article 'der'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFourteen: Enter the form (neu): Der ___ Computer ist sehr schnell.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFourteenTip: Definite article. The article 'der' already showed the gender, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFifteen: Choose the correct option: Mom bought a blue cup
definiteIndefiniteQuestOne.questFifteenTip: Feminine. After the article 'eine', the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.

definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.title: Article Logic: Finale
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.description: Mixed training. Learning to distinguish between when we know the object and when we see it for the first time.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.goal: Solidify the difference in endings once and for all!
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questOne: Enter the form (alt): Dort steht ein ___ Haus.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questOneTip: The object is mentioned for the first time (unknown). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -es ending from the article 'das'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questTwo: Enter the form (alt): Das ___ Haus ist sehr teuer.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questTwoTip: The object is already familiar (we know it). The definite article 'das' already showed everything, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questThree: Choose the correct option: In the room there is a new wardrobe
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questThreeTip: The object is mentioned for the first time (unknown). Wardrobe is masculine (der). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -er ending from the article 'der'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFour: Choose the correct option: This new wardrobe is very big
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFourTip: The object is already familiar (known). The article 'der' already showed the gender, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFive: Assemble: Mom bought a tasty pizza
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFiveTip: Object mentioned for the first time. Feminine: the adjective takes the -e ending from the article 'eine'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questSix: Assemble: This tasty pizza is still hot
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questSixTip: Object is already familiar. The article 'die' already showed everything, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questSeven: Enter the form (groß): Dort ist ein ___ Garten.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questSevenTip: Object mentioned for the first time. Garden is masculine (der). The article 'ein' is empty, so the adjective takes the -er ending from the article 'der'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questEight: Enter the form (groß): Der ___ Garten ist sehr schön.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questEightTip: Object is already familiar. The article 'der' already showed everything, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questNine: Choose the correct option: I will buy a new laptop
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questNineTip: Object mentioned for the first time. Masculine, Akkusativ. The article 'einen' has a case ending, so the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questTen: Choose the correct option: I will fix this new laptop
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questTenTip: Object is already familiar. In masculine Akkusativ, after any changed article (den), the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questEleven: Enter the form (alt): Ich habe in einem ___ Hotel geschlafen.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questElevenTip: Object mentioned for the first time but in Dativ. The article 'einem' already has an ending, so the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questTwelve: Enter the form (alt): In dem ___ Hotel war es laut.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questTwelveTip: Object is already familiar (Dativ). After the definite article 'dem', which already showed the case, the adjective takes the -en ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questThirteen: Assemble: A little child is laughing
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questThirteenTip: Object mentioned for the first time. Child is neuter (das). The article 'ein' is empty, the adjective takes the -es ending from the article 'das'.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFourteen: Assemble: This little child is laughing
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFourteenTip: Object is already familiar. The article 'das' already showed the gender, so the adjective takes the -e ending from the article.
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFifteen: Choose the correct option: He has a fast car
definiteIndefiniteQuestTwo.questFifteenTip: Object mentioned for the first time. Car is neuter (das). The article 'ein' is empty, the adjective takes the -es ending from the article 'das'.

pastValleyQuestFour.title: Inseparable Prefixes
pastValleyQuestFour.description: Prefixes like be-, ver-, er-, and others remove the ge- prefix. Remember: no 'ge-ge'!

pastValleyQuestFour.questTwo: Choose the correct answer: Did you understand everything?

pastValleyQuestFour.questFiveTip: Erzählen is a weak verb. The 'ge-' prefix is not added because the verb has an inseparable prefix 'er-'. The '-en' ending changes to '-t'.
pastValleyQuestFour.questEightTip: Erklären is a weak verb. The 'ge-' prefix is not added because the verb has an inseparable prefix 'er-'. The '-en' ending changes to '-t'.
pastValleyQuestFour.questNineTip: Verkaufen is a weak verb. The 'ge-' prefix is not added because the verb has an inseparable prefix 'ver-'. The '-en' ending changes to '-t'.
pastValleyQuestFour.questEleven: Assemble the sentence: You promised that.
pastValleyQuestFour.questTwelveTip: bestellen is a weak verb. The 'ge-' prefix is not added because the verb has an inseparable prefix 'be-'. The '-en' ending changes to '-t'.
pastValleyQuestFour.questThirteenTip: Passieren is a weak verb, but it ends in -ieren. For such verbs, the ge- prefix is never used, and the -en ending changes to -t.
pastValleyQuestFour.questFourteenTip: Erkennen is a strong (mixed) verb. The ge- prefix is not added because of the inseparable prefix er-. The root changes (e > a), but the -en ending remains.

pastValleyQuestFive.questNine: Assemble: We went to a restaurant.
pastValleyQuestFive.questNineTip: gehen is a strong verb. The ge- prefix is added, and the -en ending is kept. The root changes (geh > gang). Used with the auxiliary verb sind.
pastValleyQuestFive.questTenTip: essen is a strong verb. In Partizip II, the ge- prefix is added and the -en ending is kept. A -g- is inserted between the prefix and the root for easier pronunciation.
pastValleyQuestFive.questElevenTip: bringen is a mixed verb. It has no inseparable prefix, so ge- is added. The root changes (bring > brach), but it uses the 'weak' ending -t.
pastValleyQuestFive.questTwelveTip: vergessen is a strong verb. The ge- prefix is not added because it has an inseparable prefix ver-. The root does not change, and the -en ending is kept.

actionValleyQuestOne.title: Me, You, Him

actionValleyQuestOne.questOne: Assemble the sentence: I am helping you.
actionValleyQuestOne.questOneTip: The verb 'helfen' requires the Dative case.
actionValleyQuestOne.questThreeTip: The verb 'glauben' (to believe) requires the Dative case.

actionValleyQuestOne.questSixTip: The verb 'schenken' (to give a gift) often requires two objects: to whom (Dative) and what (Akkusativ).

actionValleyQuestOne.questThirteenTip: The verb 'geben' (to give) follows the scheme: to whom (Dative) + what (Akkusativ).
actionValleyQuestOne.questFourteen: Assemble: I want to bring you some tea.
actionValleyQuestOne.questFifteenTip: The modal verb 'sollst' is in the second position, and 'antworten' goes to the very end. Between them is the pronoun in Dative.

actionValleyQuestTwo.title: With Whom and Where?
actionValleyQuestTwo.description: Using Dative prepositions to describe your movements and plans.
actionValleyQuestTwo.goal: Practice prepositions mit, nach, zu, von, aus, bei, seit.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questOne: Assemble: I am going with a friend.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questTwo: Select: I am going to the doctor
actionValleyQuestTwo.questTwoTip: The preposition 'zu' always requires Dative. In spoken language, 'zu + dem' merges into 'zum'.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questFour: Assemble: He lives with his parents.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questFive: Select: After the course, we go home.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questSix: Assemble: I am going to the station.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questSixTip: The preposition 'zu' (to) always requires Dative. The contraction 'zu + dem' becomes 'zum'.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questEightTip: The preposition 'aus' (out of/from) always requires Dative.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questNine: Assemble: I am at my friend's (female) house.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questEleven: Assemble: We are coming from the city.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questFourteen: Assemble: He is going to the library.
actionValleyQuestTwo.questFourteenTip: The preposition 'zu' requires Dative. The contraction 'zu + der' becomes 'zur'.

actionValleyQuestThree.title: For and Through
actionValleyQuestThree.description: Practicing prepositions für, ohne, durch, gegen, um. Only direct object, only Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestThree.goal: Consolidate the use of Akkusativ after specific prepositions.
actionValleyQuestThree.questTwo: Select: I am coming without the dog
actionValleyQuestThree.questThreeTip: The preposition 'durch' (through) always requires Akkusativ. Park is 'der Park' (masculine), so the article changes to 'den'.
actionValleyQuestThree.questSix: Assemble: I am going without a key
actionValleyQuestThree.questEight: Select: Are we walking around the garden?
actionValleyQuestThree.questNine: Assemble: He is driving through the city
actionValleyQuestThree.questTenTip: The preposition 'um' (around) requires Akkusativ. Lake is 'der See' (masculine). Note: Do not confuse it with 'die See' (sea).
actionValleyQuestThree.questEleven: Assemble: I am buying this for my son
actionValleyQuestThree.questTwelve: Select: To swim against the current?
actionValleyQuestThree.questFifteen: Select: We are walking through the forest
actionValleyQuestThree.questFifteenTip: The preposition 'durch' always requires Akkusativ. Forest is 'der Wald' (masculine).

actionValleyQuestFour.title: Where to or Where?
actionValleyQuestFour.description: Learning to distinguish direction (Akkusativ) and location (Dativ) with two-way prepositions: in, an, auf, hinter, neben, and others.
actionValleyQuestFour.goal: Learn to choose the correct case based on the question: Wohin? or Wo?
actionValleyQuestFour.questOne: Select: I put the vase on the table
actionValleyQuestFour.questOneTip: If there is movement or direction (where to? wohin?), use Akkusativ. Use the corresponding Akkusativ article for the noun.
actionValleyQuestFour.questTwo: Assemble: The vase is standing on the table.
actionValleyQuestFour.questTwoTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questThree: Select: We are going to the cinema.
actionValleyQuestFour.questThreeTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFourTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ. We are already inside, there is no movement, so use the Dativ article.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFive: Assemble: I put the book in the cupboard.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFiveTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ. Set the article for the noun in Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questSix: Select: The book is lying on the shelf.
actionValleyQuestFour.questSixTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ. Set the article for the noun in Dativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questSevenTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ. Set the article for the noun in Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questEight: Select: The picture is hanging on the wall.
actionValleyQuestFour.questEightTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ. Set the article for the noun in Dativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questNine: Assemble: He sits down behind me.
actionValleyQuestFour.questNineTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ. Use the Akkusativ form for the noun or pronoun.
actionValleyQuestFour.questTenTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ. Use the Dativ form (mir) for the pronoun.
actionValleyQuestFour.questEleven: Select: The cat runs under the bed.
actionValleyQuestFour.questElevenTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ. Set the article for the noun in Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questTwelve: Assemble: The cat is sleeping under the bed.
actionValleyQuestFour.questTwelveTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ. Set the article for the noun in Dativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questThirteen: Assemble: The cat runs under the bed.
actionValleyQuestFour.questThirteenTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ. Set the article for the noun in Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFourteen: Select: We are driving to the city.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFourteenTip: If the question is 'Where to?' (Wohin?), use Akkusativ. Set the article for the noun in Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFifteen: Select: We live in the city.
actionValleyQuestFour.questFifteenTip: If the question is 'Where?' (Wo?), use Dativ. Set the article for the noun in Dativ.

actionValleyQuestFive.title: Who? To Whom? What?
actionValleyQuestFive.description: Learning to build sentences with a recipient (Dative) and an object (Akkusativ). Rule: Recipient first, then object.
actionValleyQuestFive.goal: Consolidate word order and object cases.
actionValleyQuestFive.questOne: Select: I give flowers to my mother
actionValleyQuestFive.questOneTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), we use Dative. For the noun (or pronoun), we use the Dative article.
actionValleyQuestFive.questTwo: Assemble: He gives the child an apple.
actionValleyQuestFive.questTwoTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), we use Dative. For the recipient, we use the Dative article. For the object 'What?' (Was?), we use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questThreeTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questFour: Select: We buy father a car
actionValleyQuestFive.questFourTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questFive: Assemble: She writes a letter to a friend.
actionValleyQuestFive.questFiveTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questSixTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questSevenTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ - die Regel (feminine).
actionValleyQuestFive.questEight: Assemble: We send them a gift.
actionValleyQuestFive.questEightTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questNine: Select: The waiter brings the guest soup
actionValleyQuestFive.questNineTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questTenTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ - der Saft (masculine).
actionValleyQuestFive.questEleven: Assemble: Father buys the child ice cream.
actionValleyQuestFive.questElevenTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questTwelve: Select: I tell the children a story
actionValleyQuestFive.questTwelveTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questThirteenTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ. In the neuter gender, the possessive pronoun in Akkusativ does not change its form.
actionValleyQuestFive.questFourteen: Assemble: I am returning the keys to you.
actionValleyQuestFive.questFourteenTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestFive.questFifteen: Select: We wish you much luck
actionValleyQuestFive.questFifteenTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dative. If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), use Akkusativ. The word 'viel' is used with uncountable nouns.

actionValleyQuestSix.title: Verb Government
actionValleyQuestSix.description: Who do we help, and who do we see? Practicing verbs that dictate the case themselves (Dativ or Akkusativ).
actionValleyQuestSix.goal: Practice the government of verbs danken, helfen, gefallen, etc.
actionValleyQuestSix.questOneTip: Tip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), we use Dative. There is no direct object (What?) in this sentence because 'to thank' only works with a recipient.
actionValleyQuestSix.questTwo: Assemble: He often helps his father.
actionValleyQuestSix.questTwoTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), we use Dative.
actionValleyQuestSix.questThreeTip: Problems is plural. In Akkusativ, the plural form for 'your' remains 'deine'.
actionValleyQuestSix.questFour: Select: My wife likes the dress
actionValleyQuestSix.questFive: Assemble: We must visit our grandmother.
actionValleyQuestSix.questFiveTip: If there is a question 'Whom?' (Wen?), we use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestSix.questSix: Select: The student answers the professor
actionValleyQuestSix.questEight: Assemble: Can you find my key?
actionValleyQuestSix.questEightTip: Finden requires Akkusativ: masculine changes the ending to -en.
actionValleyQuestSix.questNine: Select: The bicycle belongs to a friend
actionValleyQuestSix.questNineTip: If there is a question 'To whom?' (Wem?), we use Dative. There is no direct object (What?) in this sentence because 'to belong' only works with a recipient.
actionValleyQuestSix.questTenTip: If there is a question 'What?' (Was?), we use Akkusativ - Das Wort. 'jede+s' takes the ending from the article.
actionValleyQuestSix.questEleven: Assemble: I want to congratulate my brother.
actionValleyQuestSix.questTwelve: Select: I don't like the soup
actionValleyQuestSix.questThirteenTip: If there is a question 'What?' (Was?) or 'How long?', we use Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestSix.questFourteen: Assemble: He listens carefully to the teacher.
actionValleyQuestSix.questFourteenTip: Zuhören + Dative: the separable prefix goes to the end.
actionValleyQuestSix.questFifteen: Select: Do you need my help?

actionValleyQuestSeven.title: Trap Verbs
actionValleyQuestSeven.description: Calling, visiting, and believing. Practicing verbs where the German case doesn't match logic.
actionValleyQuestSeven.goal: Memorize the government of verbs like anrufen, besuchen, fragen, gratulieren, and others.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questOne: Choose the correct answer: I am calling my father.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questTwo: Assemble the sentence: We are visiting our grandmother.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questSevenTip: If the question is 'Whom?' (Wen?), we use Akkusativ. There is no recipient (To whom?) in this sentence, so Dativ is not used.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questEight: Assemble: I am listening to you carefully.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questEightTip: Zuhören (to listen to someone) is Dativ.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questNine: Select: I am inviting a friend.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questTenTip: Verzeihen (to forgive). If the question is 'To whom?' (Wem?), we use Dativ. There is no direct object (What?) in this sentence.
actionValleyQuestSeven.questTwelve: Select: Do you know this person?
actionValleyQuestSeven.questFifteenTip: Danken requires Dativ (dem). The word 'Kollege' adds -n in all cases except Nominativ.

actionValleyQuestEight.title: Verbs and Their Companions
actionValleyQuestEight.description: Waiting, thinking, and dreaming. Learning to use verbs with their mandatory prepositions and the correct case.
actionValleyQuestEight.goal: Memorize combinations like warten auf, denken an, träumen von.
actionValleyQuestEight.questOne: Choose the correct answer: I am waiting for you.
actionValleyQuestEight.questTwo: Assemble: I am thinking of you.
actionValleyQuestEight.questTwoTip: Denken requires the preposition an + Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFour: Select: I dream of a car.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFourTip: Träumen is always with von + Dativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFive: Assemble: I am happy about the gift (already received).
actionValleyQuestEight.questFiveTip: Sich freuen über: to be happy about something that already exists (Akkusativ).
actionValleyQuestEight.questSix: Select: I thank you for the help.
actionValleyQuestEight.questSixTip: Danken (to whom - Dat) + für (for what - Akk).
actionValleyQuestEight.questEight: Assemble: I am interested in music.
actionValleyQuestEight.questNine: Select: I am telling about the trip.
actionValleyQuestEight.questNineTip: Erzählen (to tell) usually goes with von + Dativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questTenTip: Angst haben (to be afraid) requires vor + Dativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questEleven: Assemble: I am talking with my brother.
actionValleyQuestEight.questTwelve: Select: We laugh at the joke.
actionValleyQuestEight.questTwelveTip: Lachen (to laugh at something) is über + Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questThirteenTip: Sich erinnern (to remember) requires an + Akkusativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFourteen: Assemble: He asks about the way.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFourteenTip: Fragen (to ask about something) is nach + Dativ.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFifteen: Select: I am participating in the course.
actionValleyQuestEight.questFifteenTip: Teilnehmen (to participate) is always an + Dativ.

actionValleyQuestNine.title: Masters of Replacement
actionValleyQuestNine.description: Continuing to learn how to replace entire phrases with short words. Practicing daran, wonach, wovor, and others.
actionValleyQuestNine.goal: Automate the use of pronominal adverbs in different contexts.
actionValleyQuestNine.questOne: Select: What are you asking about?
actionValleyQuestNine.questOneTip: Fragen nach: requires a question (about what?).
actionValleyQuestNine.questTwo: Assemble: I am angry about it.
actionValleyQuestNine.questTwoTip: Sich ärgern über -> answer: da + r + über (dadrüber/darüber).
actionValleyQuestNine.questThreeTip: Sprechen über -> question structure: Wo + r + über = Worüber (about what?).
actionValleyQuestNine.questFour: Select: I am used to it.
actionValleyQuestNine.questSix: Select: What do you feel like doing?
actionValleyQuestNine.questSevenTip: Zufrieden mit -> answer: Damit (with it/happy with it).
actionValleyQuestNine.questEight: Select: What are you afraid of?
actionValleyQuestNine.questEightTip: Angst haben vor: question: Wo + vor.
actionValleyQuestNine.questNineTip: Bitten um -> answer: Darum (for it/about it).
actionValleyQuestNine.questTen: Select: What are you starting with?
actionValleyQuestNine.questElevenTip: Hoffen (to hope) auf -> answer: Darauf (for it).
actionValleyQuestNine.questTwelve: Assemble: We are working on it.
actionValleyQuestNine.questThirteen: Select: I am celebrating my birthday and inviting you to it.
actionValleyQuestNine.questFifteen: Select: Shall I look after it?

actionValleyQuestTen.title: Grandmaster of Replacement
actionValleyQuestTen.description: Final grind on pronominal adverbs. Only pure German in the options.
actionValleyQuestTen.goal: Practice advanced links like woran, wovon, wozu and their replacements.
actionValleyQuestTen.questOne: Select: What are you relying on?
actionValleyQuestTen.questOneTip: Verlassen auf requires the question Wo+r+auf (Worauf).
actionValleyQuestTen.questThreeTip: Träumen von requires the question: Wovon (of what?) Wo + von.
actionValleyQuestTen.questFiveTip: Zweifeln an requires the answer: Daran.
actionValleyQuestTen.questSix: Select: What are you complaining about?
actionValleyQuestTen.questSixTip: Beschweren über requires the question Worüber (Wo + r + über).
actionValleyQuestTen.questSevenTip: Wissen + von requires the answer: Davon.
actionValleyQuestTen.questEight: Select: What are you participating in?
actionValleyQuestTen.questEightTip: Teilnehmen + an requires the question: Woran.
actionValleyQuestTen.questNine: Assemble: I am ready for it.
actionValleyQuestTen.questTen: Select: What is it made of?
actionValleyQuestTen.questTenTip: Bestehen aus requires: Woraus (Wo + r + aus).
actionValleyQuestTen.questElevenTip: Einigen auf requires the answer: Darauf.
actionValleyQuestTen.questTwelveTip: Es geht um requires the question Worum (Wo + r + um).
actionValleyQuestTen.questThirteen: Select: I am sure of it.
actionValleyQuestTen.questThirteenTip: Überzeugen von requires the answer Davon (da + von).
actionValleyQuestTen.questFourteenTip: Abhängen von requires the answer: Davon.
actionValleyQuestTen.questFifteen: Select: I congratulate you on that.
actionValleyQuestTen.questFifteenTip: Gratulieren zu requires the answer: Dazu.

actionValleyQuestEleven.title: Final Mix
actionValleyQuestEleven.description: Final challenge. All the main traps collected here: from cases and prepositions to item replacements.
actionValleyQuestEleven.goal: Remember everything and prove that the base of cases and verbs is 100% mastered.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questTwo: Assemble: I go with my friend
actionValleyQuestEleven.questThree: Select: We are walking through the park
actionValleyQuestEleven.questFourTip: When answering 'Where?' (Wo?), we use Dative. The preposition 'in' merges with 'dem' to form 'im'.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questFive: Assemble: I go to the cinema.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questFiveTip: Where to? Akkusativ. In + das = ins.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questSix: Select: I am calling my father.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questSevenTip: N-declension: Junge gets -n in all cases except Nominative.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questEightTip: When the action is on a body part: use Dative (mir).
actionValleyQuestEleven.questNine: Select: I am waiting for the bus.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questTenTip: Question for an object with 'an': it is Woran (Wo + r + an).
actionValleyQuestEleven.questTwelve: Select: The waiter brings the guest soup.
actionValleyQuestEleven.questFifteen: Select: Who are you talking to?
actionValleyQuestEleven.questFifteenTip: For people, use preposition + question (Mit wem?).

orderValleyQuestOne.title: Verb at the end!
orderValleyQuestOne.description: Practicing word order in subordinate clauses. The main rule: the verb goes to the very end.
orderValleyQuestOne.goal: Learn to place the verb in the last position after conjunctions like weil, dass, wenn, and others.
orderValleyQuestOne.questOne: Assemble: I study because it is important.
orderValleyQuestOne.questOneTip: In a subordinate clause after the conjunction (weil), the verb always takes the last position.
orderValleyQuestOne.questTwo: Select: He says that he will come.
orderValleyQuestOne.questTwoTip: The conjunction 'dass' sends the conjugated verb to the very end of the phrase.
orderValleyQuestOne.questThreeTip: Wenn (if/when) is a subordinate conjunction; the verb 'habe' stands at the end.
orderValleyQuestOne.questFour: Assemble: We go home when the movie ends.
orderValleyQuestOne.questFive: Select: I don't know if he will come today.
orderValleyQuestOne.questFiveTip: The conjunction 'ob' (if/whether) works the same way: the verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestOne.questSix: Assemble: She works although she is ill.
orderValleyQuestOne.questSixTip: Obwohl (although) is a typical conjunction for a Nebensatz. It sends the conjugated verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestOne.questEight: Select: I am tired because I get up early.
orderValleyQuestOne.questEightTip: For verbs with a separable prefix at the end of a subordinate clause, the prefix does NOT separate.
orderValleyQuestOne.questNine: Assemble: I think that you are right.
orderValleyQuestOne.questNineTip: The conjunction 'dass' (that) is a 'subordinating' conjunction. It forces the verb to move to the very end.
orderValleyQuestOne.questTenTip: Question words (wo, wann, wie) in the middle of a sentence also require the verb at the end.
orderValleyQuestOne.questEleven: Select: We know that we must help.
orderValleyQuestOne.questElevenTip: If there is a modal verb, it is the one (müssen) that stands in the last position.
orderValleyQuestOne.questTwelve: Assemble: I will call you as soon as I arrive.
orderValleyQuestOne.questTwelveTip: In the main part, the prefix 'an' separated. Don't forget that in the subordinate part, the prefix in 'ankomme' stays at the end with the verb.
orderValleyQuestOne.questThirteenTip: Damit (so that) is a subordinate conjunction.
orderValleyQuestOne.questFourteen: Select: Since it's already late, I'm going to sleep.
orderValleyQuestOne.questFourteenTip: Da (since/because). If the subordinate clause comes first, the verb in it is still at the end, and the main clause starts immediately with the verb (gehe).
orderValleyQuestOne.questFifteen: Assemble: He asked where you bought this book.
orderValleyQuestOne.questFifteenTip: In the past tense (Perfekt), the auxiliary verb (hast) stands last, after the participle.

orderValleyQuestTwo.title: Mini-phrases
orderValleyQuestTwo.description: Short phrases and sentences to practice subordinate clauses.
orderValleyQuestTwo.goal: Consolidate the verb position in subordinate clauses using simple examples.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questOne: Assemble: I know that you are here.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questOneTip: After the conjunction 'dass', the conjugated verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questTwo: Select: He eats because he is hungry.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questTwoTip: After 'weil', the conjugated verb always stands at the very end of the sentence.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questThreeTip: The conjunction 'dass' is subordinating. It forces the conjugated verb to move to the very end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFour: Assemble: I will ask if he is coming.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFourTip: The conjunction 'ob' requires the verb in the last position.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFive: Select: I don't know where my phone is.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFiveTip: In an indirect question after 'wo', the verb 'ist' must be at the very end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questSix: Assemble: We stay home if it rains.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questSixTip: After the conjunction 'wenn', the conjugated verb always stands at the end of the sentence.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questSevenTip: After the conjunction 'obwohl' (although), the conjugated verb must be at the very end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questEight: Select: I see that you are reading.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questNine: Assemble: We wait until he calls.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questNineTip: For the verb 'anrufen', the prefix does not separate because it stands at the end of the subordinate clause.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questTenTip: In a subordinate clause after the conjunction 'weil', the conjugated verb always stands at the very end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questEleven: Select: I know where you live.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questElevenTip: The question word 'wo' in the middle of a sentence works like a conjunction and puts the verb at the end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questTwelve: Assemble: I'm glad that you can come.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questTwelveTip: In a pair of two verbs, the conjugated (modal) verb is always placed after the infinitive at the very end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questThirteenTip: In a subordinate clause after 'dass', the conjugated verb always stands in the last position.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFourteen: Select: He is silent because he is tired.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFourteenTip: The conjunction 'da' (since): verb at the end.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFifteen: Assemble: I don't know when he will come.
orderValleyQuestTwo.questFifteenTip: Question words (wann, wo, wie) in the middle of a sentence send the verb to the very end.

orderValleyQuestThree.title: Nebensatz: Level Up
orderValleyQuestThree.description: Consolidating subordinate clauses. The phrases are longer now, but the rule hasn't changed: verb at the very end.
orderValleyQuestThree.goal: Practice word order in more complex sentences with circumstances and modal verbs.
orderValleyQuestThree.questOne: Assemble: I cannot come because I have to work.
orderValleyQuestThree.questOneTip: In a subordinate clause with a modal verb, the modal verb stands last. You can find the list of modal verbs in the Learn section.
orderValleyQuestThree.questTwo: Select: I'm not sure if he's coming to the party today.
orderValleyQuestThree.questTwoTip: In a subordinate clause after the conjunction 'ob', the conjugated verb is at the very end.
orderValleyQuestThree.questThreeTip: Two verbs at the end: main verb, then modal verb.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFour: Assemble: I wonder why he sold his new car.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFourTip: In the past tense (Perfekt), the verb 'hat' moves past the participle to the very end.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFive: Select: Tell me where you bought this coat.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFiveTip: In a subordinate clause (indirect question), the auxiliary verb must be at the very end.
orderValleyQuestThree.questSix: Assemble: He is tired although he slept for a long time.
orderValleyQuestThree.questSixTip: In Perfekt, the auxiliary verb must be at the very end, after the participle.
orderValleyQuestThree.questSevenTip: The conjugated verb stands at the end.
orderValleyQuestThree.questEight: Select: Do you know how much these brown shoes cost?
orderValleyQuestThree.questEightTip: The question word 'wie viel' requires the verb at the end of the phrase.
orderValleyQuestThree.questNine: Assemble: I will call you as soon as I finish eating.
orderValleyQuestThree.questNineTip: After 'sobald' (as soon as), the conjugated verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestThree.questTenTip: The modal verb stands in the very last position.
orderValleyQuestThree.questEleven: Select: Do you know when the movie starts?
orderValleyQuestThree.questElevenTip: The question word 'wann' in the middle of a sentence turns it into a subordinate clause and sends the verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestThree.questTwelve: Assemble: Do you know why she didn't come to school today?
orderValleyQuestThree.questTwelveTip: In Perfekt, the auxiliary verb stands after the participle.
orderValleyQuestThree.questThirteenTip: The conjunction 'dass' forces the verb to stand in the very last position, even after time-related words (morgen).
orderValleyQuestThree.questFourteen: Select: Tell me when you will come home.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFourteenTip: The question word 'wann' in the middle of a sentence works like a conjunction and requires the verb in the last position.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFifteen: Assemble: We are glad that you are learning German on skillupgerman.
orderValleyQuestThree.questFifteenTip: Even if a website name or other additions appear in the sentence, the conjunction 'dass' still pushes the conjugated verb to the very end.

orderValleyQuestFour.title: The Magic of 'Es gibt'
orderValleyQuestFour.description: Practicing the fixed expression 'es gibt' (there is/are). This link never changes, and whatever follows is always placed in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFour.goal: Practice Akkusativ after 'es gibt' and reinforce the fixed form of 'gibt'.
orderValleyQuestFour.questOne: Assemble: There is a park here.
orderValleyQuestFour.questOneTip: The construction 'es gibt' always requires Akkusativ. Masculine: ein -> einen.
orderValleyQuestFour.questTwo: Select: There is a museum in the city.
orderValleyQuestFour.questTwoTip: Museum is neuter (das); the article does not change in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFour.questThreeTip: In a question, the verb 'Gibt' comes first.
orderValleyQuestFour.questFour: Assemble: There are no problems here.
orderValleyQuestFour.questFourTip: Even if there are many items (Probleme), the verb 'gibt' remains singular.
orderValleyQuestFour.questFiveTip: If the sentence doesn't start with 'Es', the verb still stays in 2nd place, and 'es' moves to 3rd.
orderValleyQuestFour.questSix: Assemble: Is there a restaurant here?
orderValleyQuestFour.questSixTip: For a question, place 'Gibt' in the first position.
orderValleyQuestFour.questSevenTip: Fehler (mistake) is masculine, so use 'einen' in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFour.questEight: Select: There is milk in the fridge.
orderValleyQuestFour.questEightTip: The verb 'gibt' never turns into 'geben', even with abstract or uncountable nouns.
orderValleyQuestFour.questNine: Assemble: There is coffee for breakfast.
orderValleyQuestFour.questNineTip: Akkusativ for masculine (der Kaffee) is used without an article here, but the verb is in place.
orderValleyQuestFour.questTenTip: Standard question 'What is there today (for lunch/on the menu)?'
orderValleyQuestFour.questEleven: Select: There are many trees in the forest.
orderValleyQuestFour.questElevenTip: Plural does not affect the verb: it remains 'es gibt'.
orderValleyQuestFour.questTwelveTip: Use 'Es gibt' when saying that something exists in principle or is available.
orderValleyQuestFour.questThirteenTip: The phrase 'There is nothing / Nothing is available'.
orderValleyQuestFour.questFourteen: Select: Is there a supermarket here?
orderValleyQuestFour.questFourteenTip: Don't forget the Akkusativ for masculine gender.
orderValleyQuestFour.questFifteen: Assemble: There are many students in our school.
orderValleyQuestFour.questFifteenTip: (plural), but the verb 'gibt' is strictly singular.

orderValleyQuestFive.title: Es gibt Continued
orderValleyQuestFive.description: Practicing the 'es gibt' construction. Remember: this link never changes, and everything following it is always in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFive.goal: Automate the use of Akkusativ after 'es gibt'.
orderValleyQuestFive.questOne: Assemble the sentence: Is there an exit here?
orderValleyQuestFive.questOneTip: In a question, the order swaps. Remember Akkusativ for masculine.
orderValleyQuestFive.questTwo: Select the correct option: There is no entrance here.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFour: Assemble: There is a mistake here.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFourTip: Masculine (Fehler) gets the article 'einen' in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFive: Select: Where is there a toilet here?
orderValleyQuestFive.questFiveTip: After the question word 'Wo', the verb 'gibt' takes the second position.
orderValleyQuestFive.questSix: Assemble: There is a good reason.
orderValleyQuestFive.questSixTip: Grund is masculine. The article changes to 'einen' in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFive.questSevenTip: In a question, 'Gibt' stands before 'es'. The verb doesn't change even if there are many questions.
orderValleyQuestFive.questEight: Select: There are no classes today.
orderValleyQuestFive.questEightTip: Unterricht is masculine. Use the negation 'keinen' in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestFive.questNine: Assemble: There is nothing more for today.
orderValleyQuestFive.questNineTip: The negation 'nichts' (nothing) is not declined and is simply placed after the verb.
orderValleyQuestFive.questTenTip: Lösung (solution) is feminine; the article 'eine' does not change.
orderValleyQuestFive.questEleven: Select: Is there a pharmacy nearby?
orderValleyQuestFive.questElevenTip: For a question, put the verb 'Gibt' first.
orderValleyQuestFive.questTwelve: Assemble: There is no hope for this.
orderValleyQuestFive.questTwelveTip: After 'es gibt', it's always Akkusativ. For feminine (Hoffnung), 'keine' looks the same as Nominativ.
orderValleyQuestFive.questThirteenTip: Fixed expression: 'There is a lot to do'.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFourteen: Select: There is a letter in this bag.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFourteenTip: The construction 'es gibt' always requires Akkusativ, so the article changes accordingly.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFifteen: Assemble: There is one more chance.
orderValleyQuestFive.questFifteenTip: Chance is feminine. 'Es gibt' always requires Akkusativ.

orderValleyQuestSix.title: Reflexive Pronouns
orderValleyQuestSix.description: Distinguishing between Akkusativ and Dativ. If the action is directed toward an object (hair, teeth, hands), use the Dativ form.
orderValleyQuestSix.goal: Understand the difference between Akkusativ and Dativ in reflexive verbs.
orderValleyQuestSix.questOneTip: There is no object here, the action is simply on oneself. Use Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questTwo: Select: You are combing your hair.
orderValleyQuestSix.questTwoTip: There is an object, so the reflexive pronoun is placed in Dativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questThreeTip: In the 3rd person, the form 'sich' is always the same for both cases.
orderValleyQuestSix.questFour: Assemble: We are brushing our teeth.
orderValleyQuestSix.questFourTip: There is an object here. For 'wir', the form is the same in both cases.
orderValleyQuestSix.questSix: Assemble: I am washing my hands.
orderValleyQuestSix.questSixTip: There is an object, so it is Dativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questSevenTip: Please take a seat. The polite form 'Sie' requires 'sich'.
orderValleyQuestSix.questEight: Select: I am ordering myself a pizza.
orderValleyQuestSix.questEightTip: Pizza is a direct object. Use Dativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questNineTip: No object, action is on oneself. Akkusativ. Don't forget the separable prefix.
orderValleyQuestSix.questTen: Select: You are putting on a jacket.
orderValleyQuestSix.questTenTip: There is an object here. So it is Dativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questElevenTip: We are meeting. For 'wir', the form does not change in either case.
orderValleyQuestSix.questTwelveTip: In this case, 'sich merken' (to memorize/remember) always requires Dativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questFourteen: Assemble: You are watching a video (plural).
orderValleyQuestSix.questFourteenTip: To watch something - 'sich anschauen': requires Dativ.
orderValleyQuestSix.questFifteenTip: Hurt (whom? oneself). Akkusativ for the neuter gender.

orderValleyQuestSeven.title: Everything at Once
orderValleyQuestSeven.description: In every sentence, you must track word order in the subordinate clause, cases after 'es gibt', and reflexive pronouns.
orderValleyQuestSeven.goal: Consolidate all complex topics in a mixed mode.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questOne: Assemble: I know that there is a mistake here.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questOneTip: 'dass' throws the verb to the end, and 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questTwo: Select: He says that he is washing himself now.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questTwoTip: In a subordinate clause, the reflexive 'sich' stands immediately after the subject.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questThreeTip: Ausgang (exit) is masculine. After 'es gibt' in a subordinate clause, use Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFour: Assemble: I see that you are combing your hair.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFourTip: There is an object, so we use Dativ. The verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFive: Select: I am in a hurry because time is short.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFiveTip: The verb 'beeilen' requires Akkusativ. At the end is the 'es gibt' construction.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questSix: Assemble: I will remember that there is a mistake here.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questSixTip: 'Sich merken' is Dativ. In the subordinate clause, 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questEight: Select: We are happy that there is a solution.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questEightTip: The conjunction 'dass' sends the verb to the end, and the phrase 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questNineTip: Reflexive verb in a subordinate clause: 'sich' before the verb.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questTen: Select: I will order myself a pizza if there is a discount.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questTenTip: Ordering for oneself is Dativ. After 'wenn', the verb is at the very end.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questEleven: Select: You see that there is a problem here.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questElevenTip: The conjunction 'dass' sends the verb to the very end, and 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ after it.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questTwelve: Assemble: It is important that there is an entrance here.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questTwelveTip: In a subordinate clause after 'dass', the verb goes to the last place.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questThirteen: Select: I am happy because there is a discount.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questThirteenTip: To be happy - 'sich freuen' (Akkusativ). After 'es gibt', the verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFourteen: Assemble: I will rent myself an apartment if there is a balcony.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFourteenTip: There is an object, so it's Dativ (mir). After 'es gibt', it gets Akkusativ. Verb at the end because of 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestSeven.questFifteenTip: Subordinate clause - verb at the end.

orderValleyQuestEight.title: Travel
orderValleyQuestEight.description: Practicing everything at once regarding holidays: subordinate clauses, 'es gibt', and reflexive verbs in a travel context.
orderValleyQuestEight.goal: Consolidate word order and cases using travel examples.
orderValleyQuestEight.questOne: Assemble: I know that there is a beach here.
orderValleyQuestEight.questTwo: Select: He says that he is resting now.
orderValleyQuestEight.questTwoTip: Sich ausruhen is a reflexive verb. In a subordinate clause, 'sich' follows the subject.
orderValleyQuestEight.questThreeTip: In a subordinate clause, 'gibt' stands at the very end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFour: Assemble: He orders himself a taxi because there is no subway here.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFourTip: Ordering for oneself is Dativ. After 'da' (since), the verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFive: Select: We are happy because there is a discount on the tour.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFiveTip: After 'weil', the verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questSix: Assemble: I will remember that there is a station here.
orderValleyQuestEight.questSixTip: Sich merken: Dativ. Use the indefinite article in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestEight.questSevenTip: Airport (Flughafen) is masculine. The case after 'es gibt' is Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestEight.questEight: Select: I'm angry that there is no space.
orderValleyQuestEight.questEightTip: After 'es gibt', Akkusativ is required, and the verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questNine: Assemble: I am booking myself a room if there is a vacancy.
orderValleyQuestEight.questNineTip: Booking for oneself: Dativ. + indefinite article in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestEight.questTen: Select: You see that there is a cafe here.
orderValleyQuestEight.questTenTip: Café is neuter. After 'dass', the verb is at the very end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questElevenTip: Looking forward to something (future) — sich auf etwas freuen.
orderValleyQuestEight.questTwelve: Assemble: It's important that there is a pool here.
orderValleyQuestEight.questTwelveTip: Verb 'gibt' in the last place. + indefinite article in Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestEight.questThirteen: Select: Happy that there is an excursion.
orderValleyQuestEight.questThirteenTip: To be happy — 'sich freuen'. Indefinite article in Akkusativ. Verb at the end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFourteen: Assemble: You take a car for yourself if there is a rental here.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFourteenTip: If the question is 'To whom?' (Wem?), use Dativ. 'Wenn' sends the verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestEight.questFifteenTip: The conjunction 'dass' moves the verb to the end, and 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ. Since it's plural, the negation ends in -e.

orderValleyQuestNine.title: Work
orderValleyQuestNine.description: Interviews, deadlines, and job hunting. Practicing word order and reflexive pronouns.
orderValleyQuestNine.goal: Consolidate topics in the context of career and office.
orderValleyQuestNine.questOne: Assemble: I will apply (for the job) if there is work.
orderValleyQuestNine.questOneTip: The verb 'sich bewerben' requires Akkusativ. The conjunction 'wenn' sends the verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestNine.questTwo: Select: He says that he is introducing himself now.
orderValleyQuestNine.questTwoTip: Sich vorstellen: to introduce oneself. In a 'dass' clause, the conjugated verb is last.
orderValleyQuestNine.questThreeTip: After 'dass', the verb goes to the end, and 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFour: Assemble: I will remember that there is a meeting.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFourTip: Sich merken: to remember (Dativ). In the subordinate clause, 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFive: Select: I'm glad because there is a bonus.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFiveTip: Bonus is masculine. After 'weil', the verb 'gibt' goes to the very end.
orderValleyQuestNine.questSix: Assemble: I'm looking for a job for myself if there is a vacancy.
orderValleyQuestNine.questSixTip: When doing something for oneself (looking for, buying), use Dativ (mir). After 'wenn', the verb is last.
orderValleyQuestNine.questSevenTip: The conjunction 'ob' (whether) turns it into a subordinate clause. 'Es gibt' always requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestNine.questEight: Select: We are angry that there is no work.
orderValleyQuestNine.questEightTip: To be angry: sich ärgern. In the subordinate clause, 'dass' sends the verb to the last place.
orderValleyQuestNine.questNine: Assemble: I'll buy myself a laptop if there is a discount.
orderValleyQuestNine.questNineTip: For whom (myself) is Dativ (mir). After 'es gibt', the object is Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestNine.questTen: Select: You see that there is a problem.
orderValleyQuestNine.questTenTip: Problem is neuter. 'Dass' sends the verb to the end; 'es gibt' requires Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestNine.questElevenTip: Sich vorbereiten — to prepare. In the subordinate clause, 'sich' follows the subject.
orderValleyQuestNine.questTwelve: Assemble: It's important that there is a plan.
orderValleyQuestNine.questTwelveTip: Plan is masculine (einen Plan). After 'dass', the verb goes to the end.
orderValleyQuestNine.questThirteen: Select: I'm in a hurry because there is a deadline.
orderValleyQuestNine.questThirteenTip: Sich beeilen (to hurry) — Akkusativ. 'Termin' often means a deadline or appointment.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFourteen: Assemble: I'll take this job if there is a contract.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFourteenTip: Sich nehmen (to take for oneself): Dativ. Verb at the end due to 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestNine.questFifteenTip: Geld is neuter. The negation 'kein' in Akkusativ does not change form for neuter.

orderValleyQuestTen.title: Work: Simple and Clear
orderValleyQuestTen.description: Practicing word order and reflexive verbs on simple topics: illness, breaks, being late, and money.
orderValleyQuestTen.goal: Practice grammar with the simplest examples.
orderValleyQuestTen.questOne: Assemble: I am not working today because I am ill.
orderValleyQuestTen.questOneTip: The conjunction 'weil' sends the verb to the end of the sentence.
orderValleyQuestTen.questTwo: Select: He says he is late.
orderValleyQuestTen.questTwoTip: To be late: 'sich verspäten'. In the subordinate clause, the verb moves to the end.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFour: Assemble: I am happy that I have a day off.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFourTip: To be happy: 'sich freuen' (Akkusativ). The verb stands at the end after 'dass'.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFive: Select: I am in a hurry because there are things to do.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFiveTip: To hurry: 'sich beeilen'. In the subordinate clause, 'weil' sends the verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestTen.questSix: Assemble: I will remember that there is a meeting tomorrow.
orderValleyQuestTen.questSixTip: For whom (to oneself): this is Dative, and after the verb and 'es gibt', it is always (what?): Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestTen.questEight: Select: We are angry because there is no break.
orderValleyQuestTen.questEightTip: To be angry: 'sich ärgern'. Indefinite article in Akk.
orderValleyQuestTen.questNine: Assemble: I will buy it if there is money.
orderValleyQuestTen.questNineTip: Buying for oneself: Dative. The verb 'gibt' moves to the end.
orderValleyQuestTen.questTen: Select: You see that there is a problem.
orderValleyQuestTen.questTenTip: After 'es gibt', it's always Akkusativ, but only the masculine gender gets the -en ending (einen). 'Problem' is neuter (das), so the article does not change (ein).
orderValleyQuestTen.questElevenTip: To wash oneself — 'sich waschen'. In the subordinate clause, 'dass' sends the verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestTen.questTwelve: Assemble: It is important that there is work.
orderValleyQuestTen.questTwelveTip: In the subordinate clause (dass), the verb 'gibt' stands in the last place.
orderValleyQuestTen.questThirteen: Select: I am in a hurry because time is short.
orderValleyQuestTen.questThirteenTip: Sich beeilen (to hurry) requires Akkusativ. After 'weil', the verb 'gibt' always moves to the end.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFourteen: Assemble: I will take it if there is a receipt.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFourteenTip: Taking for oneself: Dative. After 'wenn', the verb 'gibt' moves to the end, preceded by the Akkusativ.
orderValleyQuestTen.questFifteenTip: After 'es gibt', it's always Akkusativ. For masculine gender (der Stress), the negation 'kein' must take the -en ending: 'keinen'.

orderValleyQuestEleven.title: Grammar: New Level
orderValleyQuestEleven.description: Practicing word order, reflexive verbs, and 'es gibt' in various daily situations: food, rest, shopping, and plans.
orderValleyQuestEleven.goal: Consolidate topics with fresh examples without repetition.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questOne: Assemble: I'll order myself a pizza because there's no pasta.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questOneTip: For whom (oneself): Dative; what (is/exists): always Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' goes to the end due to 'weil'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questTwo: Select: He asks if there is an entrance here.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questTwoTip: Recipient (oneself): Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'ob' (if).
orderValleyQuestEleven.questThree: Write: I rest when there is time.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questThreeTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFour: Assemble: She says she is putting on makeup now.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFourTip: Recipient (oneself): Dative (mir). In a 'dass' clause, the reflexive particle (sich) is placed immediately after the subject.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFive: Select: I'll buy myself a jacket if there's a discount.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFiveTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questSix: Assemble: It's a pity that there is no towel.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questSixTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'dass'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questSevenTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'weil'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questEight: Select: We are angry that there is no sun.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questEightTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'dass'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questNine: Assemble: I'll check the car if there's a key.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questNineTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questTen: Select: You see that there is beer.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questTenTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'dass'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questElevenTip: In a 'dass' clause, the reflexive particle (sich) is placed immediately after the subject.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questTwelve: Assemble: It is important that there is a coach.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questTwelveTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'dass'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questThirteen: Select: I am in a hurry because there is an appointment.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questThirteenTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'weil'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFourteen: Assemble: I'll get myself a coffee if there's milk.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFourteenTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestEleven.questFifteenTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'dass'.

orderValleyQuestTwelve.title: Home and Leisure: Grammar
orderValleyQuestTwelve.description: Practicing word order, reflexive verbs, and 'es gibt' in everyday situations: apartment, friends, hobbies, and relaxation.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.goal: Consolidate rules on the topic of daily life.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questOne: Assemble: I'm going to the meeting because there's a party there.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questOneTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' goes to the end due to 'weil'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questTwo: Select: He says he is watching a movie.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questTwoTip: Recipient: Dative (mir); object: Akkusativ. In a 'dass' clause, the verb moves to the end.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questThreeTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'dass'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFour: Assemble: I will think about it if there is a chance.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFourTip: Recipient: Dative; object: Akkusativ. Verb 'gibt' moves to the end due to 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFive: Select: I am putting on a white shirt because I am going on a date.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFiveTip: When naming a specific item (shirt: Hemd), we use Dative (mir). 'Weil' sends the verb to the end.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questSix: Assemble: It's a pity there's no dog here.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questSixTip: After 'es gibt', it's always Akkusativ. For masculine gender (der Hund), 'kein' must become 'keinen'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questSevenTip: The conjunction 'ob' (if) sends the verb 'gibt' to the end. 'Balkon' is in Akkusativ, so use 'einen'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questEight: Select: We are resting because there is no stress.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questEightTip: Reflexive 'uns' for 'we rest'. In 'es gibt', negation is 'kein'. 'Weil' sends 'gibt' to the end.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questNine: Assemble: I'll look at the apartment if there's a key.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questNineTip: In 'sich etwas anschauen', the pronoun is Dative (mir). 'Wenn' sends 'gibt' to the end.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questTen: Select: You see there's a mistake there.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questTenTip: 'Dass' puts 'gibt' at the end. Remember Akkusativ: 'der Fehler' becomes 'einen Fehler'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questElevenTip: The conjunction 'dass' puts 'wäscht' at the end. Since he washes 'himself' entirely, use Akkusativ — 'sich'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questTwelve: Assemble: It's important that there is a garden.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questTwelveTip: 'Es gibt' requires Akkusativ. 'Dass' sends 'gibt' to the very end.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questThirteen: Select: I am washing my hands because there is soap.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questThirteenTip: When washing a specific body part (hands), use 'mir' (Dative). 'Weil' sends 'gibt' to the end.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFourteen: Assemble: I will take the room if there is a bed.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFourteenTip: In 'sich (Dative) etwas nehmen', we use 'mir'. After 'es gibt' comes Akkusativ. 'Gibt' goes to the end after 'wenn'.
orderValleyQuestTwelve.questFifteenTip: Negation with 'es gibt' is 'kein'. After 'dass', the verb 'gibt' always escapes to the very end.

regions.descriptionWisdomSummit: The last land of B1: review the Lands of the Wise and pass the exam for all of B1.
regions.descriptionOpinionTower: Here you learn to give your opinion: Ich finde, dass…, Meiner Meinung nach…, to agree and disagree, and to guess with wird wohl.
regions.descriptionWordForge: Here you learn to make new words from words you know: die Wohnung, die Gesundheit, freundlich, essbar, unmöglich.
regions.descriptionNuanceBridge: Here you learn what makes your German more precise: zwar… aber, sowohl… als auch, indem, bis, Passiv Perfekt and participles as adjectives.
regions.descriptionLinkHarbor: Here you learn paired connectors: nicht nur… sondern auch, weder… noch, je… desto, and also statt… zu and seitdem.
regions.descriptionQuestionBridge: Here you learn verbs with prepositions: warten auf, denken an. The questions Auf wen? and Worauf? and the answer darauf.
regions.descriptionTasteMarket: Here you learn adjectives without an article: frisches Brot, heißer Kaffee, mit kalter Milch.
regions.descriptionHeroSquare: Here you learn weak nouns: den Kollegen, dem Kunden, des Studenten, Herrn Braun.
regions.descriptionOwnerCastle: Here you learn the genitive: whose? das Auto des Vaters, wegen des Regens, trotz der Arbeit.
regions.descriptionRegretRiver: Here you learn to talk about what could have happened: Wenn ich das gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen.
regions.descriptionWishIsland: Here you learn to talk about things that are not real: Wenn ich Zeit hätte, würde ich reisen.
regions.descriptionExperienceSummit: The last land of the Mountains of Experience: review everything you have learned and pass the exam.
regions.descriptionDecisionWorkshop: Here you learn fixed phrases: eine Entscheidung treffen, eine Frage stellen, Bescheid sagen, Rücksicht nehmen and more.
regions.descriptionTaskTower: Here you learn zu + infinitive (Ich habe keine Lust zu kochen, Es ist schwer, früh aufzustehen) and lassen (Ich lasse mein Auto reparieren).
regions.descriptionCraftValley: Here you learn the passive: you say what is being done, not who does it. Das Auto wird repariert.
regions.descriptionNeighborStreet: Here you learn to describe people and things: der Mann, der …; das Haus, in dem …; alles, was …
regions.descriptionConsequenceFork: Here you learn to talk about results and conditions: sodass, so … dass, falls and solange.
regions.descriptionPurposePath: Here you learn to talk about goals: um … zu, damit and the question wozu.
regions.descriptionReasonBridge: Here you learn to explain reasons and results: deshalb, darum, denn, trotzdem, obwohl.
regions.descriptionMemoryLake: Here you learn to say what had happened even earlier: hatte gegessen, war gegangen, nachdem, bevor, während.
regions.descriptionStoryValley: Here you learn to tell stories about the past like in books: machte, ging, kam, fuhr, als ich Kind war …
regions.descriptionA2Summit: The last A2 land: review everything you have learned and pass the final trial.
regions.descriptionNobodyVillage: Here you learn to talk without extra words: jemand, niemand, etwas, nichts, alles, man, einer, keiner, meiner.
regions.descriptionChoiceCrossing: Here you learn to choose and point things out: Welcher Rock? Dieser hier. Jeden Tag, alle Kinder. Was für ein Auto?
regions.descriptionAdviceGarden: Here you learn to give advice and talk about wishes: Du solltest …, Ich würde gern …, Ich wäre gern …, Wie wäre es mit …?
regions.descriptionComparisonHills: Here you learn to compare: schneller, älter, besser als, so groß wie, am größten, der schnellste Zug.
regions.descriptionTimeRoad: Here you learn to say when and for how long: vor zwei Jahren, seit drei Jahren, für eine Woche, in einer Stunde, ab Montag, bis Freitag.
regions.descriptionCalendarValley: Here you learn ordinal numbers, dates and the time: der dritte Mai, am ersten Juni, halb vier.
regions.descriptionA1Summit: The last A1 land: review everything you have learned and take the final exam.
regions.descriptionHealerHut: Here you learn the parts of the body and say what hurts: Mein Kopf tut weh. Ich habe Fieber. Ich möchte einen Termin.
regions.descriptionDressBazaar: Here you choose clothes, talk about colours and try things on in a shop: Die Hose ist blau. Das Kleid gefällt mir. Kann ich den Rock anprobieren?
regions.descriptionHeartyInn: Here you talk about food, order in a café and pay the bill: Ich mag Käse. Die Suppe schmeckt gut. Die Rechnung, bitte!
regions.descriptionPowerPass: Here you learn to say what you can do, must do and want to do, and what is allowed: Ich kann schwimmen. Ich muss arbeiten. Ich will reisen. Darf ich hier parken?
regions.descriptionRoutineMill: Here you talk about your day and learn separable verbs: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf. Am Samstag kaufe ich ein. Der Zug fährt um acht Uhr ab.
regions.descriptionClockTower: Here you learn to talk about time: days of the week (am Montag), parts of the day (morgens, am Abend), the time (Es ist acht Uhr, um neun Uhr), months and seasons (im Mai, im Sommer).
regions.descriptionFamilyTree: Here you talk about your family and say whose things are whose: mein Bruder, deine Schwester, sein Auto, ihre Tasche, unser Haus. Ich besuche meinen Onkel.
regions.descriptionChangeRiver: Here verbs change their vowel: ich fahre, du fährst, er fährt. Ich esse, du isst. Ich lese, sie liest. Only du and er, sie, es change.
regions.descriptionMarketSquare: Here you go shopping and learn the Akkusativ: Ich brauche einen Stuhl. Ich kaufe den Käse. Wir haben keinen Zucker. Wen besuchst du?
regions.descriptionQuestionGorge: Here you learn to ask questions and say “no”: Wohnst du hier? Was ist das? Wo ist die Küche? Nein, das ist nicht mein Buch. Ich habe kein Auto.
regions.descriptionMeetMeadow: Here you learn to talk about yourself and others: ich, du, er, wir, the verbs sein and haben, and how a verb changes: ich wohne, du wohnst.
regions.descriptionEastPlain: This is where the journey begins. You learn to say hello, tell your name and where you are from, count and order in a café.
regions.descriptionStoneReach: A harsh land with stony roads. Here you will strengthen your skills on the path to mastery.
regions.descriptionWindValley: The land of eternal storms and changeable weather. Gusts of wind bring trials, but along with them new knowledge. Here you face true challenges on the path of language learning.
regions.descriptionLakeRuins: Mist envelops ancient structures, and the waters of the lakes hold secrets of the past. In these lands lie forgotten knowledge that will help you delve deeper into language learning.
regions.descriptionNorthCliffs: Tall cliffs rise above the sea, and cold winds test the endurance of every traveler. Tasks requiring attentiveness await you.
regions.descriptionStormCoast: Wild coastal lands where thunder and lightning rage. Only brave heroes dare to set foot here. Here you face a true test of the power of your knowledge.
regions.descriptionMasterLands: Lands of masters and craftsmen, where every labor matters. Here you will learn how to talk about professions, work, and daily duties.
regions.descriptionWildLands: Nature is full of amazing discoveries. Here you will learn how to name forest inhabitants and elements, describe their actions, and form sentences about the natural world.
regions.descriptionPluralLands: On this steep slope, the mist of the past finally clears, revealing a view of the distant horizon. Here, the traveler learns not just to look at their feet, but to peer into both tomorrow and the days gone by.
regions.descriptionPastLands: Among the ancient stones and sands of time, stories of what has already come to pass are kept. Here, the traveler learns to look back and describe the events of yesteryear, mastering the Past Tense.
regions.descriptionActionLands: Here, time no longer stands still, and the mist of the past dissipates. In this valley, the traveler learns to set goals, mastering modal verbs and the art of interaction through grammatical cases.
regions.descriptionOrderValley: Here, the traveler learns to build proper sentences. In this valley, they master word order in simple and complex phrases, learn to report the presence of things, and use reflexive pronouns.
regions.descriptionTimeGate: Here, at the time gate, the traveler gains confidence, looking back and peering forward. In this section, we will review: the traveler revisits and consolidates the past and future tenses.
regions.descriptionEdgeImages: Adjective endings after the definite article: den alten Hund, die kleine Katze, das neue Haus.
regions.descriptionSecretLands: Adjective endings after the indefinite article: einen neuen Schrank, ein altes Schloss, in einem großen Haus.
regions.descriptionDefinite: Definite and indefinite articles together: der alte / ein alter, das neue / ein neues. Learn to choose the right adjective ending.
regions.descriptionPlacePrepositions: Here you learn to say where things are: in, auf, an, unter, über, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen and the dative.
regions.descriptionDirectionPrepositions: Here you learn to say where you are going, whose place you are at and where you come from: zu, nach, bei, aus, von, mit.
regions.descriptionActionPrepositions: Here you learn für, ohne, durch, um, gegenüber, vorbei and talk about time: am, um, im, von … bis, seit, vor, nach.
regions.descriptionPastSimple: Here you talk about the past: war, hatte, konnte, musste, wollte, durfte, sollte.
regions.descriptionRequestsLand: Here you learn to ask for things: Komm! Kommen Sie! Kannst du …? Könnten Sie …? Ich möchte … Ich hätte gern …

howToUse.title: How to use
howToUse.answerOne: To start practicing German, simply register and create an account. Without this, access to tasks will be locked.
howToUse.answerTwo: Seasonal events are temporary events tied to holidays. They feature special quests, themed tasks, and unique rewards that are only available for a limited time.
howToUse.answerThree: An achievement is a badge or marker for completed activity (progress, correct answers, daily tasks, etc.).
howToUse.answerFour: Rewards are granted for completing specific achievements and are displayed in your personal account dashboard.
howToUse.questFive: Where can I view my progress on articles?
howToUse.answerFive: On the main page under 'Member Dashboard', select 'Statistics', then choose the progress of the category you are interested in. Note: if you have no active article topics, the statistics will not be displayed.
howToUse.answerSix: Articlus is the internal currency. It is awarded for correct answers in the 'Article Practice' task and for completing tasks in Language Lands. It can be spent on extra retries.
howToUse.questSeven: How do I enter the leaderboard?
howToUse.answerSeven: The article marathon leaderboard is held once every two weeks. For two weeks, you compete with other participants. Once the marathon ends, the top three places receive achievements and rewards!
howToUse.answerEight: These are topic-based tasks that can be completed once a day. You can complete 3 tasks per day. They are available on the main page.
howToUse.answerNine: Temporary events that take place once a year. During the active period, themed tasks and rewards become available. Outside of these dates, the section is unavailable. You can check the dates in the 'Event Calendar' on the Member Dashboard.
howToUse.answerTen: Mortarboards are student hats awarded for completing daily tasks. They grant title bonuses and discounts on learning. There is a penalty system for failing to complete daily tasks.
howToUse.questEleven: Is there a penalty on mortarboards?
howToUse.answerEleven: Yes, failing to complete daily tasks results in a penalty (3 mortarboards). Complete at least one daily task to avoid the penalty. If you are away, you can buy a time freeze in the internal shop to prevent the penalty from deducting your hats!

duelGrammarTips.tipOne: Verb goes in 2nd position: Ich **lerne** Deutsch.
duelGrammarTips.tipTwo: Place or time at the beginning? Verb is still 2nd: **Heute** gehe ich.
duelGrammarTips.tipThree: Yes/No question: verb in 1st place — **Kommst** du?
duelGrammarTips.tipFour: Subordinate clause: verb at the end — …weil ich **arbeite**.
duelGrammarTips.tipFive: Conjunction **und** does not change word order: Ich lerne und ich **spiele**.

nominativ.rule: There are almost no special prepositions for the nominative. This case is usually used for the subject and after the verbs sein / werden / bleiben.
nominativ.tipOne: Nominative answers the questions Wer? / Was?
nominativ.tipTwo: After sein, werden, bleiben — the predicate noun is in the nominative.
nominativ.tipThree: If there is a preposition, it is almost never nominative.
nominativ.practiceDescription: Identify the uses of nominative without prepositions.

akkusativ.rule: These prepositions always require the accusative: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, bis, and also entlang (often as a postposition).
akkusativ.tipOne: Hack: FÜR, UM, DURCH, GEGEN, OHNE, (BIS), ENTLANG.
akkusativ.tipTwo: Movement 'to where' is often expressed with the accusative.
akkusativ.tipThree: bis is usually without article: bis Montag, bis Berlin.
akkusativ.tipFour: entlang — as a postposition: den Fluss entlang.
akkusativ.translateOne: We are walking through the park.
akkusativ.practiceDescription: Practice the prepositions that require the accusative.

dativ.rule: These prepositions always require the dative: aus, außer, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber.
dativ.tipOne: Basic set: bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu.
dativ.tipTwo: The state 'where?' is often expressed with the dative.
dativ.tipThree: gegenüber can stand after the noun: dem Haus gegenüber.
dativ.translateOne: He comes out of the house.
dativ.translateTwo: There was no one except the child.
dativ.translateSix: I have been learning German for a year.
dativ.translateSeven: The train leaves from the station.
dativ.translateNine: Opposite the house is a park.
dativ.practiceDescription: Review the prepositions that require the dative.

genitiv.rule: These prepositions require the genitive: statt, trotz, während, wegen, außerhalb, innerhalb, jenseits/diesseits, aufgrund.
genitiv.tipOne: In spoken German, the genitive is often replaced by von + dative.
genitiv.tipTwo: Articles: des/eines; nouns often get the ending -s/-es.
genitiv.tipThree: Adjectives in the genitive get the ending -en.
genitiv.translateOne: Instead of sugar I take honey.
genitiv.translateTwo: Despite the rain, we go for a walk.
genitiv.translateThree: During the lesson the phone is off.
genitiv.translateFour: Because of the cold we stay at home.
genitiv.translateFive: Outside the city it is quieter.
genitiv.translateSix: Within a week you will get an answer.
genitiv.translateSeven: On the other side of the river is a village.
genitiv.translateEight: Due to roadworks the road is closed.
genitiv.practiceDescription: Practice the use of genitive prepositions.

questLakeRuinsSixthQuests.description: The weather changes suddenly: it’s hot and sunny. You learn to talk about shade, sun protection (cream, glasses) and describe humid weather.
